claim: What a user teaches an agent (a fact, a rule, a procedure) is a typed record read conservatively from what was said
gate: no teaching read from a non-teaching (met on the first authored set, not on the second)

claim: A taught fact, correction, procedure or rule is applied in a new session; a corrected fact stays corrected; a forgotten one stays forgotten; unrelated answers are unchanged
gate: pre-registered: fact, corrected fact and procedure lower 95% bound >= 0.80 with untaught < 0.20; leak and disturbance >= 0.95; restated >= 0.95 (procedure not met)

claim: A model reads teachings that plain phrase matching misses, with few false readings
gate: found share and false-reading count on the test split of authored utterances

claim: Teaching works by voice: spoken correction, spoken confirmation, changed next answer, spoken retraction
gate: scripted spoken conversations pass their pre-registered conditions (three conversations, one synthetic voice)

claim: A fact with a name or a number taught by voice is recalled as it was meant
gate: pre-registered: lower 95% bound >= 0.80 over asks for a fact and a corrected fact, spoken in four voices (not met)

claim: A group-relative update of the synthesizer learns a planted reward faster than imitating the best take or a preference step on it
gate: held-out frames per word after twelve updates, one seed, with the recognised word error rate as guard

claim: The plain readers of spoken directives about how to speak never fire on a non-directive in an authored set
gate: false positives on the test split of authored utterances

claim: The speaking agent's first sound arrives within the planned latency
gate: first sound p50 <= 1.5 s and p95 <= 2.0 s over >=3 repeats on an idle card

claim: Speech understanding without a transcript, by a trained projector, equals the cascade
gate: equivalence on a held-out spoken set (not met)
